elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Mutuality is express and retained.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.1 reads "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000". The basis (fees paid or payable), the 12-month period and the USD 1,000,000 floor are present, but the temporal anchor is the event giving rise to the claim, not the claim itself; the deterministic check "preferred cap lookback precedes the claim" returned false and the two anchors are not to be equated.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.2 (retained verbatim): "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill..." — bilateral by "neither Party".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations", and §21.1 caps liability only "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is within Excluded Claims and therefore outside the §21.1 cap.
§21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim; §21.1 carve-out preserved.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "or fraud" within Excluded Claims, excluded from the cap by the "Except for Excluded Claims" opener of §21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: §21.3 final sentence: "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." (Narrower than model language because "Fees" is defined as the Implementation Fee, but the operative exclusion of payment obligations from capped damages exists.)

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as amended: "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim" — the edit removes the "first Order Form"/defined-"Fees" limitation that made the cap illusory (USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee), so the basis is now genuinely 12 months of fees under the Agreement.
§21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims includes "breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: The finding of deviation is correct: before the edit the cap keyed to "Fees" = the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only, which is an illusory cap below the walk-away threshold (Vendor cap under six months' fees).

Preferred level is not complete on one element only: §21.1 measures the window as the twelve months "preceding the event giving rise to the claim" rather than the twelve months preceding the claim. To reach preferred, amend §21.1 to read "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim".

Fallback level is fully met (mutual cap, 12 months' fees basis, and uncapped indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct via Excluded Claims), so the redline is position-complete at the fallback and is an acceptable landing point.

Minimality holds: only the cap basis in §21.1 was changed (removal of the "first Order Form" limitation and the defined-term "Fees" hook, plus the USD 1,000,000 floor drawn from the preferred checklist). §§21.2 and 21.3, including the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence and the full Excluded Claims list, are retained verbatim; no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added.

Intent preserved: no dangling cross-references or undefined terms are created; the defined term "Fees" remains in use elsewhere (e.g., §21.3 undisputed Fees). Optional drafting note for the comment (not a defect): using lower-case "fees" avoids the narrow §1.5 definition, and Customer may wish to say "all fees payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms" to foreclose any argument that the defined "Fees" still governs.
